param.cardRef: Card number: a display code such as ABC_0031 (case-insensitive; leading zeros may be dropped, e.g. ABC_31), or an old global number such as 114 or #114.
kanban_ping.description: Connectivity check. Returns the fixed string kanban-pong.
kanban_show.description: Show one card with its handoff, comments and status.
kanban_list.description: List cards, optionally filtered by project.
kanban_doctor.description: Read-only health check: are cards, workspaces, worktrees, branches and agents all cleaned up? Changes no state. With last set to true, returns the most recent report instead of running a new one.
kanban_comment.description: Leave a comment on a card.
kanban_complete.description: Finish an executor, reader, decision or batch card. An executor card then goes to review. When the deliverable is ready and you are waiting for a PR merge or another card, complete as usual and say what you are waiting for in the optional handoff.waitingOn; the card then shows "Waiting on external: …". For repositories without CI, run tests and the build locally before a merge and record the results in the handoff.
kanban_complete.param.handoff: The handoff must include files, verification and risks. Optional waitingOn (text), e.g. merge of PR <url>, a parent card finishing. Waiting on something external does not change what happens after completion.
kanban_block.description: Block a card only when a person is truly needed (permissions, a user decision, and so on); use kind needs_human for that. kind must be one of dependency, needs_human, capability, quota, rate_limit, transient. An executor reporting dependency for waiting on a PR or another card is refused: that is not a block; complete the card and say in the handoff what you are waiting for (handoff.waitingOn). For repositories without CI, run tests and the build locally before a merge and record the results in the handoff. When waiting for CI, complete the card and describe it in handoff.waitingOn.
kanban_approve.description: Review passed; the card moves to waiting for acceptance.
kanban_request_changes.description: Review failed: request changes. The second request for changes on the same card stops it in rework and wakes the <leader> to rule; it is not sent back to the executor automatically. The <leader> first checks the brief and scope, then rules rework, pass, or a corrected brief; if only P2 findings remain, pass and open a separate card for the leftovers. The round-3 circuit breaker (kind needs_human) is only a backstop after a ruling has sent the card back. A card returned for a land conflict does not count as a round.
kanban_create.description: The <leader> splits work into cards; investigation, testing and file changes all go to roles. Before a PR is merged, look at the diff and the review verdict yourself, write "OK to merge" on the card, then create a batch card (role=batch).
kanban_create.param.parents: Parent card numbers: display codes or old global numbers.
kanban_create.param.reviews: Review cards only: the card this review card reviews. When the review requests changes, that card goes back to rework and this review card ends. If omitted, a request for changes still goes to the <leader> for acceptance. Display code or old global number.
kanban_create.param.tags: Card tags, any number of: high-risk (a high-risk PR; the stored tier is not changed; review and the pre-start reservation both follow the executor family's L4 review list in order and take the first dispatchable profile), complex-docs (complex documentation work; explicit profile rules can route this tag to a specialist).
kanban_create.param.effort: Reasoning effort: low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Overrides the profile's own effort, and only for the agent of this card's own role. The review opened after an executor card completes still uses the review profile's own effort. Rework goes back to the original agent at the same effort.
kanban_create.param.tier: Tier: L1, L2, L3, L4. If omitted, the dispatch matrix's defaultTier applies, or L2 when there is no matrix. With high-risk and no tier, L4 applies. L4 adds high-risk automatically.
kanban_create.param.decision: Pending-decision id: d1005-091216-1 (cockpit) or k1005-091216-1 (the board's local list). Required for AFC automatic reminders (agents opened by a schedule, and cards whose title or brief contains "AFC automatic reminder"), and that decision must already be decided by the user (status done in decisions.json); optional for everyone else, and recorded in the created event when given.
kanban_link.description: The <leader> adds a parent to a card.
kanban_unlink.description: The project's <leader> or the Kanban <leader> removes parent dependencies and re-evaluates whether the card can start. Give parent or parents (at least one).
kanban_wait_user.description: The <leader> pauses a card it created: accepts ready or blocked(needs_human), atomically converting a human block to ready with a decision hold without unblock; other blocks and active cards are refused, as are human blocks with a start claim, resumable agent or unresolved parent dependency; the scheduler neither starts nor nudges it, and the board shows "Waiting for user: <decision id>". To pause a card you created, use wait-user, not block.
kanban_wait_user.param.decision: Pending-decision id: d1005-091216-1 (cockpit) or k1005-091216-1 (the board's local list)
kanban_unwait.description: The <leader> lifts "waiting for user"; the card can start as usual.
kanban_rework.description: The project's <leader> or the Kanban <leader> rules rework. Allowed from blocked, acceptance, reviewing, in_review and rework; on a card already in rework it appends a ruling. Use it to send a card stopped at round 2 back to the executor with your ruling. If the original executor is still there, the card goes back to it; if not, this round's comments are appended and the card is dispatched again in its original directory. Does not count as a review round unless countRound is true. A ruling never trips the circuit breaker by itself; the breaker on a later request for changes is only a backstop.
kanban_pass.description: The project's <leader> or the Kanban <leader> moves a card from blocked, reviewing, in_review or rework to waiting for acceptance per a ruling; it must still be accepted afterwards. Use it at round 2 when only P2 findings remain, and open a separate card for the leftovers.
kanban_accept.description: The <leader> accepts a card after looking at the diff and the review verdict yourself; clear the whole batch waiting for acceptance first. Do reversible things as recommended and list them in your report under "Decided for you (can be overturned)"; use roles decide add only for what is irreversible, costs money, touches permissions, is outward-facing, sets product direction, or needs the user to act in person. PR merging goes to a separate batch card (--role batch) with "OK to merge" written on the card. The card moves to done. A temporary workspace without a remote first lands its actual feature branch on the local base. If the main directory has uncommitted changes, acceptance still succeeds and landing is queued (land_pending). A rebase conflict first sends the card back to rework, then reports the error; this does not count as a review round. If the main directory is not on the base branch, acceptance fails and the status is unchanged. To accept an audited artifact without landing it on the local base, pass artifact as the commit, a file path, or a GitHub pull request URL, and pass reason when the evidence is a pull request. The card still has to be waiting for acceptance, with the same leader permission and, when review applies, an approving review or a lead pass. The acceptance commit, tree and evidence are recorded and the local branch is not merged or rebased. Missing evidence is refused. Having no remote does not select this mode.
kanban_accept.param.artifact: Commit, file path, or GitHub pull request URL for artifact acceptance. Omit it for ordinary acceptance. A missing remote does not select this.
kanban_accept.param.reason: What was checked. Required when artifact is a GitHub pull request URL.
kanban_reject.description: The <leader> rejects at acceptance; the card goes back to rework. Only cards waiting for acceptance can be rejected.
kanban_register.description: The <leader> registers a card for work already in progress, binding an existing agent; no new agent is created.
kanban_supervise.description: Register this session as leader of one configured project. Uses only the caller's identity. A live previous leader needs an authorized handover. Workers and scheduled agents cannot register. Registration is required before creating cards.
kanban_grant_read.description: A registered project <leader> or Kanban <leader> grants this card read access to every card in its project. Submission, completion or archive expires the grant; write permissions stay unchanged.
kanban_revoke_read.description: A registered project <leader> or Kanban <leader> revokes this card's project read grant.
